function: Per-target RIS phase customization and LSTM classification of targets from CSI, plus a learned decision on when to stop sensing, during RIS-aided communication (pp. 2, 6, 8).
system: Full-duplex BS (ULAs, Nt=Nr=2 by default), single-antenna UE, passive reflecting RIS of 20x20 to 50x50 elements, OFDM at 3 GHz, 20 MHz (pp. 3, 9-10, 12).
method: End-to-end LSTM network with a physical-channel layer and RIS phase generator, supervised cross-entropy training; softmax-temperature for discrete phases; decisioner trained by expected loss with curriculum learning (pp. 5-9).
data_channel: Own free-space multipath model with RIS and ROI voxels (p. 15); targets from MNIST, Fashion-MNIST and a released 6,000-image synthesized set; no 3GPP or measured channels (p. 9).
test_conditions: Same setup and dataset for training and testing; noise mismatch tested (trained noise-free, tested at -60 to -80 dBm), then classifier retrained in under 2 minutes (p. 11).
baselines: LISP [25] (learned, trainable RIS phases), random RIS phases [21], no RIS, GRU variant, imaging-then-CNN recognition, threshold-based stopping [29] (pp. 10-13).
metrics: Correct recognition rate on test data, average number of measurements, spectral efficiency and its loss, training time (pp. 9, 11-13).
complexity: Inference under 1 ms per instance on an Nvidia 3090 and recognition under 0.1 s; training about 210 minutes; no operation or parameter counts (p. 11).
openness: Part of the code and the synthesized dataset at https://github.com/kiwi1944/CRISense (pp. 1, 9).
q1_support: p. 9: "the CSI measurements can be generated with the physical channel model"; the model is free-space with RIS and ROI voxels (App. A, p. 15) and the targets are MNIST-type images; no 3GPP, COST 2100 or DeepMIMO model, no measured channels.
q2_support: p. 11: "originally trained with no additive noise" and tested at other noise levels, then "can be retrained with noisy measurements, which takes less than 2 minutes"; only the noise power changes (an SNR sweep), no unseen scenario, array size, dataset or band.
q3_support: p. 10: "The LISP [25] and random [21] configurations are used as comparable baselines"; "The results show significant performance improvements of our proposed NNs over both the LISP method and random configurations" (accuracy).
q4_support: p. 11: "the NN can achieve channel estimation, measurement processing, and RIS phase generation in less than 1 ms per instance when using an Nvidia 3090 GPU" (measured runtime; no operation or parameter counts).
q5_support: p. 1: "Part of the source code for this paper can be accessed at https://github.com/kiwi1944/CRISense"; p. 9: "the complete synthesized dataset can be found at https://github.com/kiwi1944/CRISense".
notes: Included as area 5 (ISAC): the learned RIS phases and sensing-duration decision serve recognition while the same downlink signal carries communication, with a time-division protocol and a spectral-efficiency loss analysis (pp. 3-4, 12-13); the RIS phases for communication come from a classical algorithm [40] (p. 4). q2 is 0 because the only mismatch tests are noise-power changes and classifier retraining (Table III, p. 11), which is an SNR sweep, and the discretized-phase variants type1 and type2 (Fig. 11, p. 12) are alternatives to the proposed quantization-aware training; reviewer may check. The released code is partial (p. 1), the dataset link is complete (p. 9).
